| 1 | Developer maintenance password `danprzjzumfgn` | `memory_0.bin` at 862 & 27977; repeated throughout `memory_2.bin` | Hardcoded credential for the "Developer Dan" account on the maintenance/development menu. Lets anyone with firmware access log in as a dev-level user. |
| 2 | Admin maintenance password `alancywupdjmydfadoaqvshshkgucnfwvvoqhjbxrdgndhfmhryjzn` | `memory_0.bin` at 27910; repeated in `memory_2.bin` | Hardcoded credential for the "Admin Alan" account, a second and higher-privilege maintenance login, also baked into the binary in plaintext. |
| 3 | `02danprzjzumfgn` (prefixed variant of the dev password) | `memory_2.bin`, immediately preceding plain `danprzjzumfgn` instances | Looks like an OTP/index prefix glued to the password (`02` + password), suggests the OTP check may just be a fixed numeric prefix rather than a real one-time code, i.e. a weak/predictable OTP scheme. |
| 4 | RSA private key, PKCS#1 PEM body (base64, no header/footer): MIIEowIBAAKCAQEA... | `memory_0.bin`, in the Dan/Alan chat log ("The key …") | A private key should never ship inside device firmware. If this is the real C&C client key, anyone who dumps firmware can impersonate the vending machine (or decrypt traffic meant for it). 2048-bit RSA private key judging by structure. |
| 5 | "Signature" base64 blob: UQVWaw374... | `memory_0.bin`, in the chat log ("The very secret signature…") | Labeled a signature but Dan notes there's no `Signed-By` field near it, it may actually be something else. Worth checking against the key above. |
| 6 | Chat log between "Alan" and "Dan" | `memory_0.bin`, start of dump | Not a technical secret by itself, but confirms: (a) the private key + signature above are real production assets, not test data; (b) a custom in-house nonce-generation function exists and was written by a non-security-aware developer, a strong candidate for a weak/predictable RNG; (c) secrets were pasted directly into code comments ("STOP SAVING OUR CONVERSATIONS IN COMMENTS"). |
| 7 | `TODO: Replace this with actual connection to C&C` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | Indicates the shipped C&C connection logic is a stub/mock. The "CONGRATULATIONS! You have successfully connected to the C&C" / "Here is the final secret:" strings sit right next to it, implying a hardcoded or trivially-bypassable success path. |
| 8 | `Signed-By: Dan` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | Hardcoded signer field. If the firmware checks this string instead of actually validating a cryptographic signature, it's a drop-in authentication bypass. |
| 9 | `Password:` / `Wrong password` / `OTP:` / `Incorrect OTP, got %s, was expecting %s` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | Confirms a password+OTP login flow exists for both the dev menu and the "vending machine number" login. The `Incorrect OTP, got X, was expecting Y` string is a classic firmware bug: if it ever prints the expected value (e.g., in a debug build) it leaks the OTP directly. |
| 10 | `DEVELOPMENT MENU` / `List Memory locations` / `Dump Memory location` / `MEMORY LOCATION TO PRINT` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | A built-in memory-dump/debug menu ships in production firmware, exactly the feature that let this analysis happen, and a direct arbitrary-memory-read primitive if reachable without full authentication. |
| 11 | `PROGMEM: Flash memory for large data` / `EEPROM: Memory for data storage` / `SRAM: Memory for runtime` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | Memory-map labels used by the dev menu above, tells an attacker which region to dump for which data (e.g., EEPROM likely holds the persisted credentials/keys). |
| 12 | `Enter password for vending machine number` / `Logged in as` / `Login failure` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | Separate per-machine login flow (distinct from the dev menu), another access-control surface worth testing. |
| 13 | `papfuarddsnrfzxuatghnxlvlayblyhxsfrfqpcsfvhpgkakzlxvy` / `arupgvxlyyrwqnberpv` | `memory_0.bin` and `memory_1.bin` | Non-dictionary strings sitting next to the credentials; pattern/length suggests they could be obfuscated (e.g., rotated/XORed) secondary secrets rather than noise. |
